problem: The dominant recipe treats fresh data as strictly better than repeated data, but for visual representation learning the repeated-epoch penalty at matched compute has not been mapped carefully against corpus quality.
core_hypothesis: With strong augmentation, a curated corpus one-tenth the size, trained for ten times the epochs, yields transfer performance within noise of single-epoch training on the full uncurated corpus at matched compute.
core_claim: With strong augmentation, a curated corpus one-tenth the size, trained for ten times the epochs, yields transfer performance within noise of single-epoch training on the full uncurated corpus at matched compute.
method_sketch: Construct nested corpus subsets by curation quality; train identical models at fixed total FLOPs across epoch-count and corpus-size trade-offs; evaluate frozen and fine-tuned transfer on a fixed downstream suite and map the iso-compute performance surface.
falsifiable_prediction: The iso-compute surface is flat within noise along the epochs-versus-corpus-size diagonal for curated data, while uncurated data shows a clear single-pass advantage.
why_important: If repetition on curated data is free, small labs can compete without web-scale collection, and dataset-size claims in pretraining papers need re-interpretation as compute claims.
why_possibly_novel: Repeated-data studies exist in language modeling, but an iso-compute epochs-versus-size map with curation quality as an explicit axis for vision pretraining is not established to my knowledge; novelty unverified.
novelty_hook: Repeated-data studies exist in language modeling, but an iso-compute epochs-versus-size map with curation quality as an explicit axis for vision pretraining is not established to my knowledge; novelty unverified.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Construct nested corpus subsets by curation quality; train identical models at fixed total FLOPs across epoch-count and corpus-size trade-offs; evaluate frozen and fine-tuned transfer on a fixed downstream suite and map the iso-compute performance surface.
main_risk: Augmentation may not substitute for data diversity at the scales tested, producing a clear repetition penalty and reducing the work to a confirmation of the default belief.
kill_risk: Augmentation may not substitute for data diversity at the scales tested, producing a clear repetition penalty and reducing the work to a confirmation of the default belief.
community_default_belief: More unique images always beat more epochs, so pretraining should maximize corpus size at fixed compute.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Strong augmentation manufactures diversity from each image, and curation removes the noise that makes extra raw data look valuable, so the unique-data advantage may be an artifact of comparing against dirty corpora.
fastest_falsifying_experiment: Train one model at ten-times epochs on the one-tenth curated subset and one single-pass model on the full corpus at equal FLOPs; a clear transfer win for the single-pass arm kills the bet.
